headline.text: The team must decide whether Google keeps putting almost all its budget into Demo. In settled campaigns Google Webinar returns $1,953 of pipeline per dollar against $612 for Google Demo, and Demo now takes 92% of Google spend.

what_happened.text: Spend fell to $17,013 across 9 campaigns, down 53% from $36,140 the week before. Clicks fell 64% and conversions fell 67% to 86.
The drop is campaigns ending, not campaigns weakening. 8 wound-down campaigns explain 99% of the spend change, and no campaign launched.
For the 6 campaigns live both weeks, spend was down 1% and CTR slipped from 2.18% to 1.97%. Conversions went from 60 to 57.
No campaigns are scheduled past Jun 30, and weekly spend is 91% below the peak week of Mar 04 ($194,291). The next launches are the chance to build tests into live spend.
Lead capture for the week is current. Qualified leads, opportunities and pipeline are provisional, because qualified leads run at only 27% of their normal rate inside the lag window.

why.text: In settled campaigns, Google Webinar out-earns Google Demo on pipeline per dollar. Google moved from 55% Webinar and 42% Demo to 5% Webinar and 92% Demo over the last 8 weeks. This is observational: it shows where to test, not what causes the gap.
Demo is below benchmark in all 3 platform cells with enough spend, and takes 49% of settled spend. Webinar is above benchmark in all 3 cells on 41% of spend.
The one test that favored Demo on Google (E013) is rejected. It ran 5 days with a sample of 31 and used a proxy metric, so it cannot support the budget move. It is the reason to re-test.

LinkedIn returns $25 of pipeline per dollar against $1,307 on Google, on a similar share of spend. 24 of 41 settled LinkedIn campaigns produced no opportunities. Last-touch attribution may under-credit LinkedIn on enterprise deals, so this is not yet proof it should be cut.
Two trusted tests (E001, E014) found ROI messaging ahead of AI Productivity, and settled campaigns agree. That question is answered, so this week's theme test goes elsewhere.

rationale.text: Google moved nearly all its budget to Demo while settled data shows Webinar returning more per dollar. The only test behind the move (E013) is rejected, so this is a clean re-test on a business outcome at full length.

experiments.expected_learning: Either way, the team learns whether Google budget should go back toward Webinar. If Webinar wins, the team repeats the test on Meta before moving more spend. If Demo wins, the current mix stays on firmer ground than E013 gave it.

creative_recommendations.text: Lead with ROI messaging for Enterprise audiences. ROI is the strongest pairing for In-House - Enterprise (1.58x) and Law Firm - Enterprise (1.52x) against comparable campaigns.
Static ROI for Law Firm (CR001) is the best performing creative at 1.45x against comparable campaigns. Use it as the shared creative in the offer tests.
Hold new Customer Proof creative work until experiment 3 reads. CR016 is the weakest creative at 0.40x, and Customer Proof for In-House - Mid-Market is among the weakest pairings at 0.64x.
Plan refreshes by platform. Meta creative holds for 6 weeks before CTR slips, and LinkedIn holds for 7 weeks. Google shows no decay with age.

CR021 (Workflow Automation, Video, Law Firm) has never run, so it is the ready fresh variant for a Law Firm rotation or format test. Security exists only in Static, so wait for a valid Security read before building Carousel or Video.

risks_and_observations.text: The week's qualified leads, opportunities and pipeline are provisional. 14 campaigns carry the immature flag, so do not judge this week on downstream results yet.

The LinkedIn holdout (SIG.07) and a LinkedIn Demo offer test get no experiment this week. The validator blocked the LinkedIn Demo arm on sample size. A holdout does not fit a one-variable design. Last-touch attribution may be hiding LinkedIn's influence on enterprise deals.

Meta and LinkedIn creative fatigue and Meta's low lead quality (only 30% of Meta leads qualify, against 63% on Google) get no test this week. Both are real exposure, but they rank below the offer and theme decisions.
The experiment log needs care. Settled campaign data disagrees with E003, E004 and E009, so none of them should drive budget until re-confirmed. E012 and E013 are overturned.

With no campaigns scheduled past Jun 30, these tests need approval and a launch slot. Nothing has been launched. Until they read on day 42, there is no valid evidence on Webinar versus Demo in Google.
